---
title: "Center Buildout Capacity"
subtitle: "Daybreak, Saratoga Springs Downtown, and The Point"
---

## Purpose

Estimate additional housing units and jobs at full buildout for three WCV
centers:

- **All three centers**: from REMM-forecast post-2025 development, applying
  each center's median dwelling-unit-per-acre and employment-density (FAR +
  job-space) assumptions to the forecast residential / commercial-employment
  development mix.
- **The Point**: additionally, from the development schedule the Point team
  has provided directly -- that schedule-based figure is the one that
  matters for The Point; the REMM-based estimate above is a cross-check.

Spatial joins, filtering, and aggregation below run in geopandas/pandas.
The base-year parcels come from `remm_base_year_data.gdb`, which is cached
as GeoParquet on first run (see below) so later runs just read that instead
of re-parsing the FileGDB.

## Centers of interest

Single ordered list to extend if more centers are added later.
`center_boundaries` is fetched in full from the REST service (no
server-side `where`), so adding a center here doesn't require touching
`sources.yml` or re-fetching -- just delete `_data/processed/centers.parquet`
to force it to rebuild with the updated list.

Every `gpd.read_file()` call below passes an OGR SQL `where` built straight
from that list, restricted to "Urban Center" polygons (drops The Point's
separate "Employment District" polygon, since every center in scope for
this analysis is its Urban Center polygon).

```{python}
CENTERS_OF_INTEREST = ["Daybreak", "Saratoga Springs Downtown", "The Point"]
```

## Load center boundaries

```{python}
from gis_adhoc_analyses.layer_cache import ensure_layers
import geopandas as gpd

L = ensure_layers(["center_boundaries"])
centers_preview = gpd.read_file(
    L["center_boundaries"],
    where=f"CenterName IN ({', '.join(map(repr, CENTERS_OF_INTEREST))}) AND CenterType = 'Urban Center'",
)
centers_preview[["CenterName", "CenterType", "City", "DwellingPerAcre", "NonResFAR"]]
```

```{python}
#| eval: false
centers_preview.explore(
    column="CenterName", tooltip=["CenterName", "CenterType", "City"], legend=False
```

## REMM parcels: load and cache as parquet

```{python}
from pathlib import Path

import geopandas as gpd
import pandas as pd

paths = {
    "raw": Path("_data/raw"),
    "processed": Path("_data/processed"),
}
paths["processed"].mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

paths.update({
    "gdb": paths["raw"] / "remm" / "remm_base_year_data.gdb",
    "buildings_2055_pkl": paths["raw"] / "remm" / "run1842year2055allbuildings.pkl",
    "progression_2055_pkl": paths["raw"] / "remm" / "run_1842_year_2055_parcel_progression_metrics.pkl",
    "parcels_geoparquet": paths["processed"] / "parcels_2023.parquet",
    "centers_geoparquet": paths["processed"] / "centers.parquet",
    "buildings_2055_parquet": paths["processed"] / "buildings_2055.parquet",
    "progression_2055_parquet": paths["processed"] / "progression_2055.parquet",
})

# one-time read of the two vector sources, cached as GeoParquet so later runs
# don't re-parse the FileGDB or re-fetch the REST layer. Each cache is a full
# replica of every source column -- selecting only the columns actually
# needed for a given step happens later, at read time (via `columns=`), not
# by trimming what gets cached here.
if not paths["parcels_geoparquet"].exists():
    parcels_gdf = gpd.read_file(paths["gdb"], layer="parcels")
    # Split_Factor/MAG_parcel_id mix strings with a couple of real NaNs, which
    # pyarrow can't write as a single column type -- nullable string dtype
    # keeps those as actual nulls (not the literal string "nan").
    parcels_gdf["Split_Factor"] = parcels_gdf["Split_Factor"].astype("string")
    parcels_gdf["MAG_parcel_id"] = parcels_gdf["MAG_parcel_id"].astype("string")
    parcels_gdf.to_parquet(paths["parcels_geoparquet"])

if not paths["centers_geoparquet"].exists():
    centers_gdf = gpd.read_file(
        L["center_boundaries"],
        where=f"CenterName IN ({', '.join(map(repr, CENTERS_OF_INTEREST))}) AND CenterType = 'Urban Center'",
    )
    centers_gdf.to_parquet(paths["centers_geoparquet"])

if not paths["buildings_2055_parquet"].exists():
    buildings_full = pd.read_pickle(paths["buildings_2055_pkl"]).reset_index()
    # 'note' mixes real strings with an int 0 sentinel (no dedicated null),
    # which pyarrow can't write as a single column type. 0 means "no note", so
    # it's replaced with an actual null rather than becoming the string "0".
    buildings_full["note"] = buildings_full["note"].replace(0, pd.NA).astype("string")
    buildings_full.to_parquet(paths["buildings_2055_parquet"])

if not paths["progression_2055_parquet"].exists():
    # no mixed-type columns here, so a plain conversion is enough
    pd.read_pickle(paths["progression_2055_pkl"]).to_parquet(paths["progression_2055_parquet"])

# only the columns needed for the spatial join below (geometry + acreage/name) --
# other columns (max_far, max_dua, DwellingPerAcre, ...) get pulled later, from
# the same cached files, only where they're actually used.
parcels = gpd.read_parquet(paths["parcels_geoparquet"], columns=["parcel_id", "parcel_acres", "geometry"])
centers = gpd.read_parquet(
    paths["centers_geoparquet"], columns=["CenterName", "CenterType", "geometry"]
).to_crs(parcels.crs)  # centers ships in EPSG:4326 (WGS84) from the REST layer; parcels are in EPSG:26912 (UTM 12N)
```

## Parcels within each center

Centroid-in-polygon join (not a straight intersection) so a parcel
straddling a center boundary is assigned to exactly one center, not
double-counted.

```{python}
# swap each parcel's polygon for its centroid point -- a polygon can legitimately
# intersect two centers along a shared edge, but its centroid falls in exactly one.
parcel_centroids = parcels.set_geometry(parcels.geometry.centroid)

# predicate="within": keep a parcel only if its centroid point falls inside a
# center polygon. how="inner" drops parcels whose centroid falls in no center
# at all (most of the region -- centers are a tiny fraction of all parcels).
parcels_in_centers = gpd.sjoin(
    parcel_centroids, centers[["CenterName", "geometry"]], predicate="within", how="inner"
)[["parcel_id", "parcel_acres", "CenterName"]]

parcels_in_centers.groupby("CenterName").agg(
    n_parcels=("parcel_id", "count"), total_acres=("parcel_acres", "sum")
)
```

## REMM developable land

Follows the original pseudocode directly: filter the 2055 buildings table
(`run1842year2055allbuildings.pkl`, one row per *building*) to parcels
within our centers of interest, keep buildings with `year_built > 2025`,
take the unique parcel ids from that, then sum `parcel_acres` for those
parcels. Computed for all three centers -- The Point's result here is a
cross-check alongside its own development-schedule-based buildout, not a
replacement for it.

An earlier version of this shortcut off the parcel-level
`parcel_progression_metrics` table instead, since it already carries a
single `year_built` per parcel. That's only valid if every building on a
parcel always shares the same year/type -- checked directly: 162 parcels
regionwide have more than one building, 2 of them are in our centers of
interest, and in both cases the buildings on that parcel happened to share
the same `year_built`. That was a coincidence of this dataset, not
something the data guarantees in general, so this now filters at the
building level as originally specified rather than relying on it holding
elsewhere.

#### (1) Restrict to parcels within our centers of interest

```{python}
# parcels_in_centers already only contains parcels inside Daybreak, Saratoga
# Springs Downtown, and The Point (centers.parquet was itself built from the
# 3-row where-filtered fetch) -- this isin() is a defensive, explicit filter
# so this cell doesn't silently depend on that upstream scoping.
our_parcels = parcels_in_centers[parcels_in_centers["CenterName"].isin(CENTERS_OF_INTEREST)]
```

#### (2) Filter the 2055 buildings table to post-2025 buildings on those parcels

```{python}
# only the columns this step needs -- year_built to filter, general_type/
# residential_units/job_spaces are read later (task 2) from the same cache.
buildings_2055 = pd.read_parquet(
    paths["buildings_2055_parquet"],
    columns=["parcel_id", "year_built", "general_type", "residential_units", "job_spaces"],
)

# inner join: only buildings whose parcel_id is one of our centers' parcels survive.
buildings_in_centers = buildings_2055.merge(
    our_parcels[["parcel_id", "CenterName"]], on="parcel_id"
)

# a parcel can have multiple buildings (see note above) -- .unique() collapses
# "one row per building built after 2025" down to "one row per qualifying parcel".
post_2025_parcel_ids = buildings_in_centers.loc[
    buildings_in_centers["year_built"] > 2025, "parcel_id"
].unique()

post_2025_parcel_ids
```

#### (3) Sum developable acreage for those parcels, per center

```{python}
developable_land = (
    our_parcels[our_parcels["parcel_id"].isin(post_2025_parcel_ids)]
    .groupby("CenterName")
    .agg(n_parcels=("parcel_id", "count"), dev_acres=("parcel_acres", "sum"))
    .reset_index()
)
developable_land
```

### Forecast development mix and buildout capacity

All three centers -- The Point's REMM-based estimate here is a cross-check
alongside its own development-schedule-based buildout (below), not a
replacement for it.

```{python}
# our_parcels/post_2025_parcel_ids are already scoped to all of
# CENTERS_OF_INTEREST from task 1 -- kept explicit in case task 2's
# center scope ever needs to differ from task 1's again.
task2_parcel_ids = our_parcels.loc[
    our_parcels["CenterName"].isin(CENTERS_OF_INTEREST)
    & our_parcels["parcel_id"].isin(post_2025_parcel_ids),
    "parcel_id",
]

task2_parcel_ids
```

#### (1) Forecast residential : commercial/employment development ratio

Sum `residential_units` and `job_spaces` from `parcel_progression_metrics`
for the post-2025 developable parcels identified above (2055 run). These
two fields were checked directly against the buildings table and are
reliable per-parcel sums across all of a parcel's buildings (unlike
`year_built`, which only reflects one representative building) -- see note
above. Full buildout of each center is assumed to follow this same mix, so
each center's total developable acreage (from task 1) is allocated between
residential and commercial/employment by this ratio.

```{python}
progression_2055 = pd.read_parquet(
    paths["progression_2055_parquet"], columns=["parcel_id", "residential_units", "job_spaces"]
)

dev_mix = (
    our_parcels[our_parcels["parcel_id"].isin(task2_parcel_ids)][["parcel_id", "CenterName"]]
    .merge(progression_2055, on="parcel_id")
    .groupby("CenterName")[["residential_units", "job_spaces"]]
    .sum()
)
dev_mix["unit_job_ratio"] = dev_mix["residential_units"] / dev_mix["job_spaces"]

# res_share/nonres_share are the same ratio re-expressed as shares of a whole
# (res_share = unit_job_ratio / (unit_job_ratio + 1)) -- this is what actually
# gets multiplied against acreage below.
dev_mix["res_share"] = dev_mix["residential_units"] / (dev_mix["residential_units"] + dev_mix["job_spaces"])
dev_mix["nonres_share"] = 1 - dev_mix["res_share"]
dev_mix
```

```{python}
# split each center's total developable acreage (task 1) into a residential
# and a non-residential/employment share, using the res_share/nonres_share
# computed above -- this is the "assume full buildout follows this same mix" step.
acreage_allocation = developable_land.set_index("CenterName").loc[
    CENTERS_OF_INTEREST, ["dev_acres"]
].join(dev_mix[["res_share", "nonres_share"]])
acreage_allocation["res_acres"] = acreage_allocation["dev_acres"] * acreage_allocation["res_share"]
acreage_allocation["nonres_acres"] = acreage_allocation["dev_acres"] * acreage_allocation["nonres_share"]
acreage_allocation
```

#### (2) Apply density assumptions to each acreage share

**Median dwelling-units-per-acre and FAR.** `max_far`/`max_dua` live on the
`parcels` table (per-parcel zoning capacity, not a text range), so this
takes the statistical median across *all* parcels in each center -- not
just the post-2025 developable ones, since the assumption is about the
center's overall zoned capacity, not only what's forecast to redevelop.
Josh noted REMM's own FAR/DUA-driven numbers assume a parcel develops
wall-to-wall (no roads, parking, or common space carved out), so if that
assumption changes later, override the values directly here (e.g.
`capacities.loc["Daybreak", "median_far"] = 2.0`) and rerun from this cell
down.

```{python}
# our_parcels only has parcel_id/parcel_acres/CenterName -- pull max_far/max_dua
# from the same parcels cache (already scoped to our_parcels via the merge).
capacities = (
    our_parcels.merge(
        gpd.read_parquet(
            paths["parcels_geoparquet"], columns=["parcel_id", "max_far", "max_dua", "geometry"]
        ),
        on="parcel_id",
    )
    .groupby("CenterName")[["max_far", "max_dua"]]
    .median()
    .rename(columns={"max_far": "median_far", "max_dua": "median_dua"})
)
capacities  # The Point's median_dua is NaN -- none of its parcels have a max_dua entitlement yet; left as-is
```

**Median employment density, from FAR and a job-space assumption.**
`sqft_per_job` (needed to turn FAR-driven building sqft into a job count)
comes from each center's own non-residential buildings (all of them, not
just post-2025 -- there aren't many non-res buildings in Saratoga Springs
Downtown yet, so restricting to post-2025 only left a very thin sample).
It turns out to be a fixed constant per building `general_type` region-wide
(Office 633, Retail 374, Industrial 975, ...), so the median here reflects
each center's non-res building mix rather than sampling noise.

```{python}
buildings_full = pd.read_parquet(
    paths["buildings_2055_parquet"], columns=["parcel_id", "general_type", "sqft_per_job"]
).merge(our_parcels[["parcel_id", "CenterName"]], on="parcel_id")

# residential building types excluded here -- sqft_per_job only makes sense
# for the non-residential/employment share of buildout.
nonres_buildings = buildings_full[
    (buildings_full["CenterName"].isin(CENTERS_OF_INTEREST))
    & ~buildings_full["general_type"].isin(["SF Residential", "MF Residential"])
]
sqft_per_job = nonres_buildings.groupby("CenterName")["sqft_per_job"].median().rename("sqft_per_job")
sqft_per_job
```

#### (3) Estimate additional housing units and jobs at full buildout

```{python}
SQFT_PER_ACRE = 43_560

capacity = acreage_allocation.join(capacities[["median_dua", "median_far"]]).join(sqft_per_job)
# residential: acres x dwelling-units-per-acre = additional housing units
capacity["housing_units"] = capacity["res_acres"] * capacity["median_dua"]
# non-residential: acres x FAR x sqft/acre = total building sqft at full buildout
capacity["nonres_sqft"] = capacity["nonres_acres"] * capacity["median_far"] * SQFT_PER_ACRE
# building sqft / sqft-per-job = additional jobs
capacity["jobs"] = capacity["nonres_sqft"] / capacity["sqft_per_job"]
capacity[["dev_acres", "res_acres", "nonres_acres", "housing_units", "jobs"]]
```

## The Point: full buildout

No separate development schedule document was ever provided, and The Point
is already REMM-modeled -- so "the development schedule" here means REMM's
own full-buildout simulation for The Point's parcels. Unlike tasks 1/2,
this doesn't need acreage allocation or density assumptions: REMM's
simulated buildings already give unit/job counts directly, so this is just
a sum, plus a check that nothing's left undeveloped (rather than an
estimate of it).

#### (1) The Point's parcels, with full-buildout attributes

```{python}
# residential_units/job_spaces here are absolute totals as of the 2055 run
# (not "_added" deltas) -- i.e. REMM's full-buildout state, not "new since 2025".
# developable/year_built/max_far/max_dua are pulled too, for the check in step (2).
point_progression = pd.read_parquet(
    paths["progression_2055_parquet"],
    columns=["parcel_id", "residential_units", "job_spaces", "developable", "year_built", "max_far", "max_dua"],
)

point_parcels = parcels_in_centers[parcels_in_centers["CenterName"] == "The Point"]
point_buildout = point_parcels[["parcel_id", "parcel_acres"]].merge(point_progression, on="parcel_id")
```

#### (2) Confirm no developable land remains (a check, not an estimate)

```{python}
# developable == 1 would mean "still vacant and buildable as of 2055" -- expect
# none, confirming there's no residual land to separately estimate.
still_developable = point_buildout[point_buildout["developable"] == 1]
print(f"parcels still flagged developable: {len(still_developable)}")

# parcels with no building recorded (year_built == 0) are only a gap if they
# also have real zoning capacity -- if max_far/max_dua are both 0 too, they're
# non-buildable infrastructure (roads, open space), not missed development.
unbuilt = point_buildout[point_buildout["year_built"] == 0]
print(f"parcels never built ({unbuilt['parcel_acres'].sum():.1f} acres), of which zero-capacity:",
      ((unbuilt["max_far"] == 0) & (unbuilt["max_dua"] == 0)).sum(), "/", len(unbuilt))
```

#### (3) Report The Point's full buildout

```{python}
point_capacity = point_buildout[["residential_units", "job_spaces"]].sum().rename({
    "residential_units": "housing_units", "job_spaces": "jobs"
})
point_capacity
```
